newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends up despite loose funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends up despite loose funds.

text.p: Taiwan's interbank rate closed slightly higher on Monday as some major financial institutions absorbed funds from the banking system despite a generally loose liquidity, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate closed at 5.799 percent against Saturday's 5.608 close -- only slightly outside the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5 percent -- with 30-day commercial paper stabilising at 5.55-5.60 percent against 5.55-5.65.
Dealers attributed the rise of interbank rate to an unequal distribution of funds in the banking system.

Unidentified financial institutions faced a money shortage even though the banking system's overall liquidity was loose due to expected maturation of some T$24 billion worth of negotiable certificates of deposit this week, dealers said.
The interbank rate may rise further on Tuesday, dealers said.
The government bond yields wavered in a narrow consolidation. No trade was reported in the afternoon.
